newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply up on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply up on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher on Saturday as investors hunted for bargains following losses in the previous two sessions, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 60.13 points, or 0.89 percent higher, at 6,826.06.
Turnover was an active T$43.88 billion.
The market had lost over 150 points on Thursday and Friday combined after South Africa announced late Wednesday it would switch diplomatic recognition to Beijing from Taipei by the end of 1997.
But the falls attracted buying from investors on Saturday who felt the Pretoria fallout would not affect Taiwan's economy, brokers said.
"The falls on Thursday and Friday were mostly psychology driven and the shock reaction is now over," said Joe Chiou, a senior analyst for Taiwan Securities Investment.
"But the rebound (on Saturday) was limited and the market is still facing resistance to a breakthrough rally," Chiou said.
Textiles and electronics paced the rise on Saturday, gaining 2.18 percent and 1.47 percent respectively.
Chia Hsin Live soared by the daily seven-percent limit, or T$0.95, to T$14.60. Compal Electronics also closed limit-up, gaining T$4.50 to T$70.50.
Brokers expected the index to consolidate at the current level next week. A 6,780-6,860 range was seen for Monday.
